audit.why: EVEN 5.5/10 is right at 49.69% over 1753 games: Irelia wins the lane on paper but Void Shift and a point-and-click suppress keep every commit honest.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns on the page. Nether Grasp is 140s at rank 1 down to 80s at rank 3, Call of the Void is a flat 6s, Malefic Visions 11s at rank 1.
audit.why: A 140-second ultimate is the largest step-up window in the matchup and the page never said so.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, breakdown.feeding, dontsFull[1].d and report[5].t now carry the numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction was never stated: Void Shift grants CROWD CONTROL IMMUNITY as well as damage reduction, so Flawless Duet's stun does nothing until damage has stripped it. Also unstated: Call of the Void SILENCES at 900 range, which locks out Bladesurge and the stun; Nether Grasp is a channel your stun cancels; and Malefic Visions jumps to a new target on a kill.
audit.why: Stunning first into an intact Void Shift is the single most common way this lane is lost, and the page's advice pointed straight at it.
audit.corrected: Added to phases[0].why, phases[2].why, phases[4].why, breakdown.mid, dontsFull[0].d, dosFull[1].d and breakdown.carry.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two kit errors: spikes[0].text names 'Null Zone', which is not in Malzahar's current kit, and early/whys[0] call Void Shift a shield that 'only mitigates one instance of damage'. Riot's text describes damage reduction plus CC immunity that lingers briefly after he takes damage. spikes[1].text also says to bait his ult with 'W's damage reduction' — Defiant Dance reduces physical damage, and Malzahar deals magic.
audit.why: Both descriptions would have the reader plan around mechanics that do not exist.
audit.corrected: spikes[0].text, spikes[1].text, early and whys[0] rewritten from the kit text.

audit.whatIsWrong: All seven phases[N].side read 'Skill' while every content win[N] reads 'Irelia'.
audit.why: Packet levelChart is Irelia on all seven rows and the content layer agrees, so the full-layer side tokens were stale.
audit.corrected: All seven aligned to Irelia with ratings and whys rewritten in the same proposal; win[N] already matches.

edits.before: Q the low minions and keep the blade moving — your level 1 reset dance already out-trades careless mages.
edits.after: Q the low minions and keep moving — Void Shift makes him CC-immune, so break it with damage before you stun.

edits.before: W joins: the channel shreds incoming damage — hold it for his trade spell, not his autos.
edits.after: W joins, but Defiant Dance cuts physical damage only — everything Malzahar has is magic.

edits.before: E completes the engine: the stun into stacked-passive autos is half a health bar at 3. Mid lane rarely budgets for it.
edits.after: E completes the engine: strip Void Shift with an auto first, then the stun lands and your Q reset chases him down.

edits.before: Reset-dance the wave into his face: four stacks, E-stun, Q the kill threat. The lane is a minion-count quiz.
edits.after: Reset-dance the wave into his face: four stacks, E-stun, Q the kill threat. Nether Grasp is not online yet.

edits.before: Vanguard's Edge online — the all-in caps with a wall of disengage-proof marks. Dive with the wave as your fuel.
edits.after: Vanguard's Edge online — and Nether Grasp is a channel, so a stun cancels the suppress the moment he starts it.

edits.before: First item spike: stacked trades delete mages and your sustain mocks their poke math.
edits.after: First item spike: stacked on-hit trades beat his Malefic Visions tick every time.

edits.before: Late Irelia surfs the fight: Q-reset through their line, stun the carry pair, and shred whoever peels.
edits.after: Late you dive him: Q-reset through their line, and a stun cancels Nether Grasp before it takes anyone.

edits.before: Malzahar wins by landing Nether Grasp, denying your pattern, and renting you the lane at a range markup.
edits.after: Malzahar wins by silencing the dash with Call of the Void, then suppressing you in Nether Grasp for the channel.

edits.before: - Malzahar Nether Grasp: matchup-defining — Point-and-click suppression — never step up solo while his passive shield is intact and R is up. Check it before every step-up. - W Defiant Dance is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Nether Grasp is 140s at rank 1 and 80s at rank 3, and it is a channel — your stun cancels it. - Call of the Void is a flat 6s silence at 900 range; eat it before you dash, never during. - Malefic Visions is 11s at rank 1. - Void Shift ignores CC until damage strips it.

edits.before: First item onward, the wave is a weapon: crash it into all-ins, R the disengage, and surf the side-lane resets between objectives.
edits.after: Strip Void Shift with an auto or a minion Q first — until it drops he ignores your stun entirely, and a 900-range silence eats the dash.

edits.before: If Malzahar takes first blood, tighten up: Nether Grasp is now always up in your head. A second kill means the duel is over and the game isn’t — farm with Q resets and stay relevant through stacked windows.
edits.after: If Malzahar takes first blood, respect the 900-range silence on Call of the Void — it locks your dash out entirely. Farm with Bladesurge resets and step up only once his 140s Nether Grasp is spent.

edits.before: Carry through the dance — the wave funds dives no cooldown can, and your R turns skirmishes into no-exit interviews.
edits.after: Carry through the dance — Flawless Duet cancels Nether Grasp mid-channel, so his one teamfight button dies to your stun.

edits.before: Ahead, dance louder: crash waves into Malzahar's face, stun the answers, and surf resets through every river fight.
edits.after: Ahead, crash the wave into Malzahar: he owns no dash, so every stun once Void Shift is stripped is a free kill.

edits.before: Point-and-click suppression — never step up solo while his passive shield is intact and R is up. Bait it, count it, then go.
edits.after: Nether Grasp is 140s at rank 1 and it channels — break Void Shift with damage first, then stun him out of the suppress.

edits.before: Q-reset through two low minions onto his chest, four-stack autos, E-stun the retreat — the wave-funded all-in he budgeted zero for.
edits.after: Malefic Visions ticks damage over time and jumps to a new target on a kill — track the number, not the bar, before you dive.

edits.before: That is Malzahar’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: Void Shift gives CC immunity — your stun does nothing until damage strips it.

edits.before: Your dashes live in the wave's health bar — shoving mindlessly is deleting your own mobility.
edits.after: Call of the Void is a flat 6s silence at 900 range — eating it means no Q, no E, no exit.

edits.before: Dashing in under-stacked with W down — Irelia without the engine is a melee minion with a famous haircut.
edits.after: His voidlings chip you the whole time you shove — clear them or your health bar funds Malefic Visions.

edits.before: Track Malzahar’s Nether Grasp: Point-and-click suppression — never step up solo while his passive shield is intact and R is up. The whole green-light system is its cooldown.
edits.after: Track Malzahar’s Nether Grasp: 140s at rank 1 and it is a channel, so your stun cancels the suppress outright — but Void Shift blocks all CC until damage strips it first.

edits.before: Ahead, dance louder: crash waves into Malzahar's face, stun the answers, and surf resets through every river fight.
edits.after: Ahead, crash the wave into Malzahar: he owns no dash, so every stun once Void Shift is stripped is a free kill.

edits.before: Malzahar has no early trading tool beyond his passive shield and DoT, so your melee pressure wins level 1 skirmishes
edits.after: Malzahar has no early trading tool beyond Void Shift and his DoT, so melee pressure wins level 1 once damage strips it

edits.before: Malzahar's Void Swarm and Null Zone deal steady poke but he has nothing to punish your Q dash — once you're inside his silence range you can burst him before Malefic Visions ticks twice.
edits.after: Malzahar's Void Swarm and Malefic Visions deal steady chip but he has nothing to punish your Q dash — once damage has stripped Void Shift you can burst him before the visions tick twice.

edits.before: His Nether Grasp is a suppress-and-burst combo, but you can bait it out with W's damage reduction or simply avoid overextending right as he hits 6, since your all-in doesn't depend on your own ult.
edits.after: His Nether Grasp is a suppress-and-burst channel, but Flawless Duet cancels it outright, so hold the stun for his commit instead of avoiding level 6 — your all-in doesn't depend on your own ult.

edits.before: Malzahar is a lane bully through DoT and voidling zoning, not through burst trades, so at level 1-2 you can walk up and punish him in melee range before his Void Swarm covers the gap. His passive shield only mitigates one instance of damage, and once it's gone your auto-Q combo deals more damage per second than his ability rotation. He has to play passively and farm from range, which cedes you lane priority early.
edits.after: Malzahar is a lane bully through DoT and voidling zoning, not through burst trades, so at level 1-2 you can walk up and punish him in melee range before his Void Swarm covers the gap. Void Shift gives him heavy damage reduction and CC immunity until he takes damage, so land an auto to strip it before you count on your stun; after that your auto-Q combo out-damages his rotation. He has to farm from range, which cedes you lane priority early.

notes: Biggest correction: Void Shift grants CROWD CONTROL IMMUNITY, not just a shield. The page told the reader to lead with the stun; against an intact Void Shift the stun simply does not apply. Every relevant field now says strip it with damage first. Also removed 'Null Zone' (not in his current kit) and the claim that Defiant Dance baits his ult (W reduces physical damage; Malzahar is magic). Chart aligned to Irelia across both layers, matching the packet. breakdown.wave and breakdown.early left templated.
